behaviour: A bare ?, ?HELP, ?help or an empty function line prints the top-level command reference.
gap: '??' (the form the page itself advertises) and a mixed-case ?Help (not matched: it answers 'Unknown command') are unasserted.
how: Send '??' and '?Help' on W1 USB; expect the reference header for the first and 'Unknown command: Help' for the second.

behaviour: A function command ending in '?' prints help instead of running: '?VERB?' prints that verb's page, '?VERB,args?' prints the top-level page, and nothing changes.
how: wcb.help_trap sends ?LABEL,S4,HILTRAP? and ?LABEL?; asserts the header / the LABEL section and that no label was set.

behaviour: MGMT, SEQ, FUNCCHAR, CMDCHAR, DELIM and WIFI (any letter case) are exempt from the trailing-'?' help shortcut, so '?DELIM,?', '!FUNCCHAR,?' and a FRAG ending in '?' reach their handlers.
gap: SEQ,SAVE with a value ending in '?', ?CMDCHAR,? (refused by prefixCharOk, not eaten), ?WIFI,...? and a mixed-case verb (?Mgmt,FRAG,...? / ?Seq,SAVE,...?) are unasserted; '?DELIM?' still printing help is unasserted.
how: Send ?SEQ,SAVE,HILQ,abc? and expect 'Stored: Key=' with value 'abc?'; send ?Seq,SAVE,HILQ2,x? (mixed case) the same; send ?CMDCHAR,? and expect the '?' collision refusal; ?DELIM? must print the DELIM page.

behaviour: Each of the 30 topic pages prints on ?<TOPIC>? (DEBUG, MAP, BAUD, LABEL, BCAST, KYBER, ETM, MAC, EPASS, WCB, WCBQ, MAESTRO, MP3, DFP/DFPLAYER, HCR, WLED, MGMT, OTA/OTALOCAL, VAR, SEQ, STATS, WIFI, WDP, DELIM, FUNCCHAR, CMDCHAR, NVS, ERASE, LED, HW).
gap: Only the corrected lines of DEBUG, BAUD, LABEL, ETM, MAC, WCB, MAESTRO, VAR and the LABEL usage line are asserted; BCAST, STATS, DELIM, FUNCCHAR, CMDCHAR, LED, MAP, NVS, ERASE, HW, KYBER, MP3, DFP, HCR, WLED, MGMT, OTA, SEQ, WIFI, WDP, EPASS, WCBQ pages are never requested.
how: For every topic send ?<TOPIC>? and assert its 'Usage:' (or first Description) line and that the top-level header does NOT print; one test, one table of (topic, line).

behaviour: The DEBUG help page lists ON/OFF, MAESTRO/KYBER, PWM, ETM and the test knobs but not the RAW, MGMT and HCR ON/OFF forms the parser accepts (the top-level page lists ?DEBUG,RAW).
gap: Doc/parser mismatch: no test asserts the DEBUG page names every accepted sub-command.
how: Send ?DEBUG? and assert lines for RAW,ON/OFF, MGMT,ON/OFF and HCR,ON/OFF; the firmware page needs the three lines added first (re-scan #29 pattern).

behaviour: A trailing-'?' request whose text is not a topic prints the top-level reference (the else branch).
how: wcb.help_trap's ?LABEL,S4,HILTRAP? reaches printCommandHelp with a non-topic and asserts the header.

behaviour: handleSingleCommand routes a token by its first character using the LIVE characters: function identifier -> processLocalCommand, command character -> the ';' family, anything else -> broadcast.
how: Covered: under '!' a '?' line is broadcast to S2; under ':' a ';' line is broadcast and ':S0' runs.

behaviour: An unrecognised function verb prints 'Unknown command: <text>' and 'Type '? ?' for help' instead of being swallowed.
how: Covered for ?ZZHIL, the removed ?TRACK family, ?STAT, ?SBAUDS1,9600, ?S69600 and a mixed-case legacy verb.

behaviour: The fixed line WCB_WEBTOOL_CONFIG_PULL prints the backup whatever the function identifier is.
how: Covered: sent under FUNCCHAR '!' and DELIM '|', the two chains print.

behaviour: An IF token that reaches the executor is dropped with '[IF] ... reached the executor with nothing to gate'.
gap: Unreachable code: the chain splitters consume every IF token before enqueue.

behaviour: A line is split on the delimiter into trimmed tokens; empty tokens are skipped; each token is enqueued in order.
how: Covered: ;S1a^;S1b^;S1c arrives in order; a^b from a port becomes two broadcasts.

behaviour: A token starting '***' is not run: 'Ignored chain command: ***...' prints and nothing goes out (chain splitter and timer walker alike).
how: Covered on the console, on a port, inside a mapping and under IF.

behaviour: A ?CS or ?SEQ,SAVE value ends only at delimiter+funcChar (so '^;' inside it is kept) and ?MGMT,... is always the final, unsplit token.
gap: Straddles the sequences and mesh slices.
how: Covered: 'xseq,save,' with a letter identifier, lowercase '?seq,save,', a value holding ;T300, FRAG payloads holding '^'.

behaviour: A '?FUNCCHAR,<c>' token inside a chain changes which prefix the rest of that chain is matched with (the factory restore chain flips mid-way).
how: Covered: the factory chain under '!' restores with its ?FUNCCHAR,! token and a stored sequence after it.

behaviour: A chain whose last token is ^<funcChar>CHK<crc> (or ^?CHK, any case, found with lastIndexOf) runs only when the CRC-32 of the text before it matches (%08X); a mismatch prints FAILED + 'Aborting restore' and runs nothing.
how: Covered: a verified one-line restore applies a label; a wrong CRC prints the FAILED and ABORTED lines (s31:573).

behaviour: A checksum written unpadded by firmware <= 6.0.x (fewer than 8 hex digits, leading zero nibble stripped) is left-padded and still verifies.
gap: No test sends a chain whose CRC has a leading zero nibble in its short (unpadded) spelling.
how: Search markers until ';S0<t>' has a CRC starting with '0'; send '<chain>^?CHK<7-digit crc>' and expect 'checksum VERIFIED' and the echo; same through the ?C branch with '?CONTROLLER^;S0<t>'.

behaviour: A console line starting ?C/?c takes its own checksum branch: a verified chain is split and run (not enqueued whole), FAILED prints Provided/Calculated, and a chain with no CHK goes through the timer-aware normal path.
how: Covered: ?CONFIG^?VERSION^?CHK runs both; ?CONTROLLER^;S1a^;T800^;S1b keeps its delay; ?CSHILCK2,..^?CHK00000000 prints 'FAILED!' with both CRCs.

behaviour: A chain whose payload legitimately contains an earlier '^?CHK' (a stored sequence value) is verified against its FINAL token only, and the verified half is not re-entered into the gate.
gap: No test stores a sequence whose value holds '^?CHK' and restores a checksummed chain carrying it.
how: Send '?SEQ,SAVE,HILCHK,;S0a^?CHKdead^;S0b^?CHK<real crc>' and expect VERIFIED and ?SEQ,GET,HILCHK to return the whole value.

behaviour: A ?-first chain carrying both a ;T token and a ?CHK token is NOT a timer chain: after verification its ;T token answers 'Invalid Serial Command' and the rest runs at once (characterisation).
gap: Unasserted characterisation: a verified checksummed chain cannot carry delays.
how: Send '?VERSION^;S1a^;T800^;S1b^?CHK<crc>'; expect 'Invalid Serial Command' once and a and b within ~100 ms of each other (pins the limitation).

behaviour: verifyBackupChecksum ('Checksum verification command received.') has no caller.
gap: Dead code.

behaviour: The 200-slot command queue discards a token it cannot take with one 'Command queue is full! Discarding command.' line per token (loop-task and WiFi-task producers never wait).
how: Covered: a 250-token port chain gives executed + discarded = 250; a 210-command recall is refused whole.

behaviour: serialCommandTask (and only it) waits up to 2 s for queue room, so a pasted USB line of more than 200 tokens runs every token.
how: Covered: 250 ;S0 tokens on one USB line all echo in order with no 'queue is full' line.

behaviour: An enqueue whose malloc fails prints 'Out of memory while enqueuing command!'; loop() drops an item whose String copy came back empty with 'Out of memory: dropped a N-character command.'
gap: Needs a heap fault knob.

behaviour: loop() restores each item's ESP-NOW origin, sequence-body flag and lineage before dispatch, so a broadcast's mesh copy and a recall's fan-out are decided per command, not from a global another task may have changed.
how: Covered: typed lines reach the mesh while W2 sends a command every 50 ms; a mesh-triggered body still broadcasts.

behaviour: ;T<ms> (or ;t) between commands delays the next group by that many ms, counted from the previous group's dispatch.
how: Covered on the console, from a stored sequence and over the mesh (~1500 / 800 ms gaps measured on the wire).

behaviour: Consecutive delay tokens with no command between them add up, a comment token between them included.
gap: The comment-between-delays case (;t500^***note^;t300^cmd waits 800) is unasserted.
how: Send ';S1a^;T600^***n^;T600^;S1b' and expect a->b about 1200 ms.

behaviour: ;T<ms>,<command> starts a group whose first command is the payload; the next plain token joins that group.
how: Covered: b about 600 ms after a, c right after b.

behaviour: A delay above 1800000 ms is capped to 30 min with 'Delay capped to 1800000 ms : originally requested N ms' always, plus the 'Warning: Delay exceeds...' line only under ?DEBUG; exactly 1800000 is not capped.
how: Covered with debug on and off, 1800001 and 1800000.

behaviour: A negative delay (;T-1, ;t-500,cmd) refuses the whole chain with 'Timer refused: ... Nothing in this chain was run.' and runs none of it.

?STOP stops the running chain and prints 'Timer sequence manually stopped.': as a typed whole line (any case), inside a plain chain, as a sequence body, from the mesh, and as the FIRST command of a timer group; ?STOP with arguments is 'Unknown command'.
gap: A ?STOP placed as a timer GROUP's first command (;S1a^;T500^?STOP^;S1b stopping at that group) and the lowercase '?stop' whole-line form are unasserted; '?STOP,x' -> 'Unknown command' unasserted.
how: Send ';S1a^;T500^?STOP^;S1b': expect a, the stop line about 500 ms later and never b; send '?stop' during a 2.5 s chain and expect the stop line; '?STOP,x' expects 'Unknown command: STOP,x'.

behaviour: Only one timer chain runs at a time: a new chain (typed, recalled or received) replaces the running one and prints 'Timer sequence replaced mid-run - N remaining group(s) ... dropped'.
how: Covered: typed and recalled replacement, and ten mesh chains in a burst.

behaviour: A chain starting with the function identifier is a timer chain only when some token is a real <cmdChar>T<digit> and no token is a CHK; it then keeps its delay instead of printing 'Invalid Serial Command'.
how: Covered: ?VERSION^;S1a^;T800^;S1b and the ?C branch; a reassembled two-chunk FRAG.

behaviour: A ';'-first or un-prefixed line is treated as a timer chain whenever ';T' or ';t' appears ANYWHERE in it (isTimerCommand), so a plain text line such as 'set;temp' takes the timer engine: it still runs (one 0-delay group) but REPLACES a running timer chain and prints 'replaced mid-run'.
gap: Unasserted: an unrelated text line containing ';t' silently kills a running show.
how: Start ';S1a^;T3000^;S1b', then type the plain line 'x;ty' 500 ms later: expect 'x;ty' broadcast, the 'replaced mid-run - 1 remaining group' line, and b never arriving (characterisation to pin or fix).

behaviour: A chain carrying ?SEQ,SAVE, ?CS or ?MGMT never goes to the timer engine: a ;t inside the value is stored, not run.
how: Covered: an IF-gated ?SEQ,SAVE with ;T stores the whole value and runs none; a FRAG payload keeps its ;T for the target.

behaviour: Each timer group fires with the source port the chain was typed on: the source skip, ?BCAST,IN blocking and the port's serial mapping all still apply.
how: Covered: ';T100^text' on S3 never echoes to S3, is blocked by IN,S3,OFF and obeys a mapping.

behaviour: A ;T chain arriving over ESP-NOW (ETM, plain, single- or multi-chunk FRAG) is queued (8 slots of 220 bytes, a heap buffer for longer) and parsed in loop() with its origin and body flag kept.
how: Covered: ~800 ms gaps on W2's port, a 260-character chain whole, origin kept across the delay.

behaviour: A received chain the 8-slot queue cannot take, or that no heap can hold, is counted and loop() prints '[TIMER] N received timer chain(s) not run: 8 already waiting' / '...no memory for the chain'.
gap: The 'no memory' arm needs a heap fault knob (WP59 pattern); only the 'already waiting' arm is driven.
how: The full-queue arm is covered by ten client chains while loop() prints ?backup; the no-memory arm needs a knob.

behaviour: A chain ending in a delay with no command after it (;S1a^;T2000) completes at once: the trailing delay is dropped silently and a following chain prints no 'replaced mid-run'.
gap: Unasserted characterisation.
how: Send ';S0a^;T3000' then ';S0b' 300 ms later and then ';S0c^;T100^;S0d': expect no 'replaced mid-run' line and d about 100 ms after c.

behaviour: Under ?DEBUG,ON each fired command prints '[TimerGroup n] Executing command: <cmd>' and the end prints 'Timer command sequence complete.'
gap: Diagnostic lines unasserted.
how: Under ?DEBUG,ON send ';S0a^;T200^;S0b' and expect '[TimerGroup 1] ... ;S0a', '[TimerGroup 2] ... ;S0b' and the complete line, in order.

behaviour: An IF inside a timer token (;t200,IF,...) is rejected with its error and the token ignored; a false IF drops a bare ;T or a ';T,cmd' token (variables slice).
gap: Straddles the variables/IF slice.

behaviour: ;S<1-5>[,]<text> writes the text plus one CR to that port, strips one optional comma after the digit, trims the payload and never flushes.
gap: The payload's own trim (';S1  x  ' writes 'x\r') is unasserted.
how: Send ';S1,  <t>  ' and expect exactly '<t>\r' on the probe.

behaviour: ;S0[,]<text> prints the text on USB.
;S6-;S9 answer 'Invalid serial port number. Must be between 0 and 5 (0=USB).'; a non-digit port (';SX,text') parses as port 0 and prints on USB (toInt).
gap: The non-digit-port -> USB quirk is unasserted.
how: Send ';SX,<t>' and expect '<t>' on USB with no error (pins the characterisation).

behaviour: A ';S' token goes to the serial writer only when its second character is not e/E: ';SEQ<key>' recalls a sequence, any other ';Se...' and a bare ';S' answer 'Invalid Serial Command'; the 'Invalid serial message format.' guard is unreachable.
gap: Bare ';S' and ';Set' -> 'Invalid Serial Command' unasserted; the length<2 guard is dead (WP59 wcb.cmd.dead_dispatch_code).
how: Send ';S' and ';Setx' and expect 'Invalid Serial Command' for both and nothing on any port.

behaviour: An unknown ';' verb (;Z..., ;T outside a timer chain, ;WHOAMI) answers 'Invalid Serial Command'.
gap: Only asserted negatively (serial.timer_after_func_command, client_mesh.whoami_roundtrip check its absence).
how: Send ';Zx' and expect the line once.

behaviour: Under ?DEBUG,ON a ;S write prints 'Sent to <port label>: <text>' / 'Sent to USB: <text>' (the label from ?LABEL).
gap: Diagnostic line unasserted (s26 only filters it).
how: Under ?DEBUG,ON with a label on S5, send ';S5x' and expect 'Sent to Serial5 (<label>): x'.

behaviour: ;W<d><payload> takes ONE digit as the target and the rest (digits included) as payload; ';W<digits>,<payload>' takes the whole digit run (two-digit targets); payload commas are kept.
A bare ;W/;w prints '[;w] usage: ;w<target|alias>,<command>'; an alias with no comma prints the alias-form line.
;W<alias>,<cmd> resolves through the WDP table case-insensitively; the board's own alias runs locally; an unknown alias prints 'No board named'; an ambiguous one is refused.
gap: The 'No board named "x" is known - see ?WDP,LIST' line is only implied (wdp.forget_floor_relearn checks routing fails).
how: Send ';Wnosuchboard,;S0x' and expect the exact 'No board named' line and no [ETM] Sent.

behaviour: ;W<own number>,<cmd> runs the command locally (enqueued, origin local) and sends nothing.
gap: Only the own-ALIAS form is asserted; the numeric self form (';W1,;S0<t>' on W1) is unasserted.
how: On W1 send ';W1,;S0<t>' under ?DEBUG,ETM,ON: expect '<t>' on USB and no '[ETM] Sent seq'.

behaviour: A target that is not an active peer or the enabled controller answers 'WCB n is not a reachable target - it isn't a configured or learned peer[ or the controller].'
how: Covered for a number above the floor and for forgotten learned peers.

behaviour: ;W2,a^b sends only 'a' to W2 and runs 'b' locally (the splitter runs before routing).
An IF inside a ;W payload is refused with '[IF] ERROR: IF cannot be routed inside ;w'.
gap: Variables slice.

behaviour: A ;W<controller>,{json} opens the 20 s RC telemetry relay window; a text route never does.
gap: NaviCore/mesh slice.

behaviour: Un-prefixed text goes to every port except the source, ports with OUT off, a configured Maestro port (and S1 under Maestro_Remote), the Kyber local port, PWM output, MP3, DFPlayer and HCR ports; a WLED port is not excluded once its output is on.
how: Covered per exclusion with output forced on.

behaviour: With ?BCAST,IN,Sx,OFF plain text from that port prints 'Broadcast blocked from SerialN (input blocking enabled)' and goes nowhere; ; and ? commands still run.
?BCAST,OUT,Sx,OFF removes only that port from the fan-out; ;Sx still writes.
With ?BCAST,OUT,S0,ON every broadcast is echoed on USB, including ones typed on USB and ones received over the mesh; a blocked one is not.
A locally originated broadcast goes to the mesh once; one that arrived over the mesh (or a FRAG with unicast origin) is never sent back; a Wizard FRAG counts as local origin.
The mesh decision is taken from the origin restored for this command BEFORE the local ports are written, so a command received mid-write cannot drop the typed line's mesh copy.
how: Covered: 30 lines under a 50 ms command load, control arm first.

behaviour: A '{' line from a port is delivered locally and sent untracked; a line over the CHKSM limit is delivered locally and refused on the mesh with the '[ETM] Command N chars exceeds' line.
gap: Mesh slice for the send side.

behaviour: Under ?DEBUG,ON a broadcast prints 'Broadcasting command:', 'Sent to SerialN:', 'Skipping Sn (Maestro/MP3 Trigger/DFPlayer/HCR port)', 'Sent to S0/USB:' and 'Broadcasted via ESP-NOW:'.
gap: Only 'Broadcasting command:' is asserted; the Sent/Skipping/Broadcasted lines are not.
how: Under ?DEBUG,ON with a DFPlayer on S5, broadcast <t> and assert the Skipping S5 (DFPlayer port) line and one 'Sent to SerialN' per written port.

behaviour: ?BCAST,IN|OUT,Sx,ON|OFF sets and saves the flag, prints 'Broadcast INPUT/OUTPUT on Sx: Enabled/Disabled'; only exact ON enables, only the port digit is read, letter case is free; missing fields, a bad direction and a port outside 1-5 print their lines.
?BCAST,OUT,S0,ON|OFF sets the USB echo and saves; ?BCAST,IN,S0 is refused as 'S0 = OUT only'.

?BCAST,RESET (and legacy ?RESET_BROADCAST) clears the bdcst_set namespace, re-enables all five ports both ways (device ports included), turns the S0 echo off, persists BOTH namespaces and prints the Created lines and the Done line.
gap: S0 echo being turned off, the 'Done. Broadcast output re-enabled ...' line and survival of the reset across a reboot are unasserted (bcast_reset_persists only re-reads ?config; reset_legacy checks the chain and one port).
how: With ?BCAST,OUT,S0,ON and IN,S3,OFF set, send ?BCAST,RESET: expect the Done line, the chain to hold OUT,S0,OFF and IN,S3,ON, then reboot W1 and expect the same chain and a typed broadcast NOT echoed on USB.

behaviour: ?SBISxON/OFF, ?SBOSxON/OFF, ?SBOS0ON/OFF and the deprecated ?Sx0/?Sx1 reach the setters with their own lines; ?SBOx1 / ?SBIx0 and out-of-range ports are refused.
Broadcast output flags (bdcst_set S1-S5, S0) and input blocking (bcast_block) load at boot and show in the banner and chain.
how: Covered: explicit OFF flags survive a reboot in the chain and on the wire.

behaviour: When NVS refuses the write, the flags still apply live and the board says 'NVS could not store the broadcast output/input flags (full? see ?NVS) - they revert at the next reboot'.
gap: The opt-in nvs_fill tests cover labels, baud and mappings, not the two broadcast namespaces.
how: Under nvs_fill (s31 pattern) send ?BCAST,OUT,S5,OFF and ?BCAST,IN,S5,OFF: expect both warnings, the live effect, and the flags back ON after a reboot.

behaviour: ?config shows 'Broadcast Blocking:' rows (with labels) and the per-port 'Broadcast Input/Output' columns from the RAM tables.
?BAUD,S1|S2,<rate> reprograms the UART live, updates the RAM table, saves serial_baud and prints 'Baud rate for SerialN updated to <rate>'.
how: Covered: bytes follow the new rate at once.

behaviour: ?BAUD,S3-S5 ends and re-begins the software UART live (95-byte RX, RMT TX) while every reader skips the port; the RMT/RX mode lines print under ?DEBUG.
how: Covered at every rate 110-115200 and under input, raw traffic and mesh chunks.

behaviour: ?BAUD refuses a missing rate or port ('Invalid format'), a port outside 1-5 (named), a rate off the table (no 4800), a soft port above 115200, and warns for a soft port above 57600 while applying it.
A PWM input or output soft port stores the rate but is not re-begun (its pin stays PWM).
gap: PWM slice.

behaviour: applyLiveBaud drains the S1/S2 TX queue before changing the divisor, so ';S2<120 chars>^?BAUD,S2,19200' leaves the line whole at the old rate.

?BAUDSx,rate reaches updateBaudRate; ?BAUDSx without a comma prints its usage; ?S<1-5><rate> is accepted with a deprecation warning and says 'stored in NVS' only when the rate was taken; other ?S... spellings are 'Unknown command'.
Saved rates load at boot into the port rows of the banner and the chain.
gap: Boot sanitising of a stored 0 is an attended OTA item (hil_plan 'A, M').
how: Covered: banner rows match the chain after a reboot.

behaviour: When NVS refuses the rate the port still runs at it and prints 'NVS could not store it (full? see ?NVS) - SerialN goes back to its saved rate at the next reboot'.
gap: Opt-in (nvs_fill).

behaviour: updateSerialSettings' 'baud' branch and updateSerialBaudRate are unreachable (isLegacySerialSetting admits digits only).
gap: Dead code.

behaviour: ?LABEL,Sx,<text> trims the text, refuses more than 30 characters ('Label too long. Maximum 30 characters.'), saves serial_labels and prints "SerialN label set to: '<text>'"; 30 exactly is stored.
?LABEL,CLEAR,Sx clears one label ('SerialN label cleared'); ?LABEL,CLEAR,ALL clears all five in order then 'All serial labels cleared'; a cleared label leaves the chain.
?LABEL,Sx with no text, an unknown form, a bad CLEAR target and a port outside 1-5 (set or clear) each print their own line and change nothing.
?SLSx,<label> and ?SLCSx reach the setters with their own port/format lines and the same 30-character cap.
A label survives a reboot, can be set on another board with ;W2,?LABEL, and shows in the chain, ?config and the banner.
When NVS refuses a label the RAM copy is unchanged and 'NVS could not store the SerialN label (full? see ?NVS) - label unchanged' prints instead of the confirmation.
gap: Opt-in (nvs_fill).

behaviour: ?MAP,SERIAL,Sx,dest[,dest...] / Sx,R,dest / SxR,dest / LIST / CLEAR,Sx / CLEAR,ALL and ?MAP,CLEAR,ALL are dispatched; a bare R, a missing destination, S0/S6 inputs, a non-S source and ?MAP,FOO print their exact lines and leave no mapping; letter case is free.

Destinations are Sx or WxSy (W0Sx = Sx, case-insensitive); duplicates are skipped with a line; WCB > 20 or port > 5 is refused (toInt quirks: 'W2S' -> W2S0, 'S-1' -> 255); an R suffix is stripped; the 11th destination is dropped silently.

A ?MAP,SERIAL for an input replaces its whole destination list; a command whose destinations are all invalid leaves the existing mapping untouched and takes no slot ('No valid destinations - SerialN mapping left unchanged').

A mapping is refused on a PWM input port, a PWM output port, and an HCR / MP3 Trigger / DFPlayer port ('Cannot create mapping: ...'); 'Maximum serial mappings reached' cannot occur (5 slots for 5 ports).
gap: 'Cannot create mapping: Port is used for PWM input' and the MP3 / DFPlayer input refusals are unasserted (only the PWM-output and HCR lines are).
how: With a PWM mapping S3->S4 live send ?MAP,SERIAL,S3,S5 and expect the PWM-input line; with ?MP3,S5 (then ?DFP,S5) send ?MAP,SERIAL,S5,S4 and expect the device line; LIST stays empty.

behaviour: A new mapping records the port's current flags, blocks its input and disables its output (printing both 'Auto-' lines once; a re-issue is idempotent); CLEAR,Sx and CLEAR,ALL put the recorded flags back, printing only what changed.

In text mode an un-prefixed line from the input goes once to each destination in list order: local ports with CR, S0 on USB, a remote port as an ACKed ETM ';S

' unicast (a leading ',' is doubled so it survives), the board's own WS

locally, a remote S0 on that board's console; ? and ; tokens still run, *** is ignored, ^ splits; over the CHKSM limit the remote copy is refused; the input port gets no broadcasts.

In raw mode RawSerialForwardingTask forwards bytes verbatim in chunks of up to 64: local and own-WCB ports and S0 in place, remote ports as raw ESP-NOW frames (no ETM, no ACK, no stats change), a remote S0 refused at configure time, with '[RAW]' hex lines under ?DEBUG,RAW and a send-failure line for an unreachable board; the command reader stays off the port; the task skips the Kyber port, a Maestro get-query port and a port being re-begun.
gap: The task's Kyber-port skip (a raw mapping whose input is the Kyber local port) and its maestroQueryPort skip are unasserted.
how: On a Kyber_Local board map the Kyber port raw to S4 and inject bytes: expect them forwarded by the Kyber path only, never doubled on S4; run a Maestro get on a raw-mapped Maestro port and expect the reply not to leak to the destination.

behaviour: Mappings, raw flags, destination lists and the recorded prior flags load at boot (missing prior-flag keys default to ON/unblocked); CLEAR then reboot leaves none.

The save writes _act last, erases every serial_map key no active mapping uses (a clear frees 6 + 2 per destination; a shrink frees 2 per dropped destination), keeps old output keys when the count could not be stored, and says 'NVS could not store it (full?)'.
gap: Last one opt-in (nvs_fill).

behaviour: ?SMSx[R],dest / ?SMLIST / ?SMRSx / ?SMCLEAR / bare ?SM reach the same functions with their lines.

?MAP,SERIAL,LIST prints 'Mapping n: SerialX[ (RAW)] -> d1, d2' or 'No serial mappings configured'; ?config and the boot banner carry the same rows; ?backup normalises the token to ?MAP,SERIAL,Sx[,R],...

Mesh bytes for a soft port are queued (16 slots of 196) for MeshSerialOutTask on core 1; a full queue drops and counts, the task reports '[SOFTSERIAL] mesh-to-port queue full: dropped N chunk(s), M in total' and holds a chunk while its port is re-begun.
The serial_monitor namespace (serialMonitorEnabled, mirrorToUSB, mirrorToKyber) and setSerialMappingRawMode are loaded/printed but settable by no command.
gap: No command writes these.

behaviour: ?DEBUG,ON|OFF, MAESTRO|KYBER,ON|OFF, PWM, ETM, HCR, MGMT and RAW ON|OFF flip RAM-only flags with their confirmation lines; anything else prints 'Invalid DEBUG command. Use: ?DEBUG ?'.
gap: The 'MGMT debugging enabled/disabled' and 'HCR debugging enabled' lines of the new form, and lowercase '?debug,on', are unasserted; RAM-only is proven only by config_guard's byte-identity.
how: One table test: send each ?DEBUG,<sub>,ON then OFF and assert the exact line; after ?DEBUG,ON reboot W1 and expect no 'Processing input' line for a typed command.

behaviour: ?DON/?DOFF, ?DMON/?DMOFF (= ?DKON/?DKOFF), ?DPWMON/OFF, ?DETMON/OFF, ?DHCRON/OFF flip the same flags.
?DEBUG,PULLFAULT,OOM|LINE|OFF, PULLPART,<n|0|OFF> and SEQNVS are RAM-only test knobs with range checks.
gap: Mesh/sequence slices.

behaviour: 'Processing input from SerialN: <line>' prints under ?DEBUG,ON except for a ?MGMT line, which prints only under ?DEBUG,MGMT; a ?STATS,RPT echo rides ?DEBUG,MGMT.
gap: That a ?MGMT line typed on USB under ?DEBUG,ON prints NO 'Processing input' line (and does under ?DEBUG,MGMT) is unasserted.
how: Under ?DEBUG,ON send '?MGMT,FRAG,2,xx,0,1,;S0x' and expect no 'Processing input from Serial0: ?MGMT'; under ?DEBUG,MGMT,ON expect it.

behaviour: ?LED (or ?LED,PIN) prints 'LED pin: GPIO<n>' and the usage; ?LED,PIN,<n> outside 0-48 is refused with no NVS write.
?LED,PIN,<n> saves led_config, re-initialises the NeoPixel on the new pin (test pixel then idle), and the next boot prints 'LED pin override from NVS: GPIO<n>'.
gap: Only the board's OWN pin is sent (no visible change); the LED actually moving to another GPIO is an attended, camera-checked item.
how: Attended: ?LED,PIN,<other free GPIO> with a LED wired there, check it lights, then ?LED,PIN,<own> back.

behaviour: ?LED,PIN,abc (or an empty value) parses to GPIO 0 and is SAVED and applied: a typo moves the status LED to GPIO0 and persists.
gap: Probable defect (misc.led_query_invalid's docstring warns against it); nothing asserts a refusal.
how: (should) Send ?LED,PIN,abc and expect a refusal with led_config unchanged in ?NVS; restore ?LED,PIN,<own> in a finally.

behaviour: ?STATS prints the unicast summary (ETM per-board sums, or the plain counters with ETM off), PWM and Raw sections when non-zero, the Heap line, ESP-NOW-drop / ETM-refused / USB-RX-overflow lines when non-zero, the per-board ETM table and the 'Reported by Other Nodes' rows.
?STATS,RESET / ?STATSRESET zero every counter, the refused count and the reported rows, printing 'ESP-NOW statistics reset.'

?STATS,RPT,<from>,<8 counters> stores one row silently (strtoul, exact above 2^31), rejects fewer than 8 fields or a reporter outside 1-20 with its line, echoes only under ?DEBUG,MGMT, keeps rows in RAM only, and does not hold off a deferred restart.
CR, LF, CRLF and LFCR each end exactly one line; whitespace-only lines do nothing.
An unterminated line waits in its port's buffer; each of the six ports assembles its own line; leftover bytes make the next line on that port a plain broadcast.
Leading and trailing spaces and tabs are trimmed from every line before dispatch.
A NUL byte (a UART break) is dropped: the command after it runs and a NUL-only line broadcasts nothing.
A port line over 4096 characters is dropped whole with one '[SERIAL] Sn: line longer than 4096 characters - dropped' line, the buffer is released, its head never runs, and the next line runs.
A USB line is capped at 32 KB; one the heap cannot grow is dropped whole with '[SERIAL] S0: line too long for the free heap (N characters) - dropped' instead of running its head unverified.
gap: The 32768 cap itself (a longer USB line on a board whose largest free block exceeds 32 KB) is unreachable in AP mode and skip-guarded; only the heap-failure arm is driven.
how: On a WiFi-OFF board (largest block > 32 KB) send a 33 KB ;S0 chain and expect the 'longer than 32768 characters' line and no token echoed.

behaviour: Several lines in one burst and a ^ chain typed on a port run in order.
A ? command typed on a port answers on USB and never on a port.

The command reader skips MP3, DFPlayer and HCR ports, the Kyber local port, a local Maestro port a bridge task drains, a Maestro get-query port, a port being re-begun and raw-mapped ports; under Maestro_Remote S1 is not read; under Kyber_Local the other hardware port still is.
gap: Device-slice straddle.

behaviour: A line starting '@WDP' on S1-S5 is handed to the WDP-DA parser and never run as a command; on USB it is ignored.
gap: WDP slice.

behaviour: USB RX ring is 8192 bytes; FIFO/ring overflows are counted by onReceiveError and shown in ?STATS as 'USB/S0 input: N RX overflow(s) - bytes were lost'.

S3-S5 receive through a 95-byte software-serial buffer (300-character lines intact, exact to 38400, 8N2 accepted, wrong-baud input never executes, exact under soft TX) and transmit through RMT at every table rate, idling HIGH from boot.
A WebSocket line is trimmed and run through processSerialCommandHelper with the WS source id (one per loop pass).
gap: WiFi slice.

behaviour: ?reboot prints 'Reboot queued' and restarts only once the command queue has been empty and quiet for 4 s ('Rebooting now...'), never under a running config pull; after 20 s of commands that keep arriving it restarts anyway with 'Restart held off N s ...'; dirty learned peers are flushed first.
how: Covered (every WCB.reboot() asserts both lines; the cap and the pull hold have their own tests).

behaviour: A ?STATS,RPT store and a ?RTERM,START re-arm to the same relay do not restart the quiet window.
Once the restart is decided no ETM command is ACKed, so a sender retries after the reboot.
gap: Mesh slice.

behaviour: ?DELIM,<c> and legacy ?D<c> set the delimiter live, save command_config, split later chains on it, reshape the backup, and the new delimiter loads at boot.

The delimiter may not be the function identifier, the command character, ',', a letter or digit, a control byte or DEL, nor more or fewer than one character; each refusal has its line and the delimiter stays.
?FUNCCHAR,<c> and legacy ?LF<c> set the function identifier live and in NVS; '?' can be restored through the exempt form; the character loads at boot and the backup chains reflect it.
The function identifier may not equal the command character or the delimiter, nor be a control byte, DEL or more than one character; ?LF longer than 3 characters is not a setter.
gap: The delimiter-collision arm ('?FUNCCHAR,|' after ?DELIM,|, or '?LF|') is unasserted: only '?' vs ';' and the format/printable arms are.
how: Set ?DELIM,| then send ?FUNCCHAR,| and ?LF| (each arrives whole since '|' now splits... send them as the only token) and expect "'|' is the command delimiter" and the identifier unchanged; restore ?DELIM,^.

behaviour: ?CMDCHAR,<c> and legacy ?CC<c> move the ';' family live and in NVS; the old ';' lines become broadcasts; the character loads at boot.
The command character may not equal the function identifier or the delimiter, nor be a control byte, DEL or more than one character; ?CCLEAR,ALL is not a setter.
gap: The delimiter-collision arm ('?CMDCHAR,^' - arrives as '?CMDCHAR,' and is refused by format, so test it with a non-default delimiter: ?DELIM,| then ?CMDCHAR,|) is unasserted.
how: Set ?DELIM,| then send ?CMDCHAR,| alone on a line and expect the delimiter-collision line and ';' unchanged; restore ?DELIM,^.

behaviour: ?config prints 'Delimiter Character:', 'Local Function Identifier:' and 'Command Character:' from the live values.
Legacy verbs match only their all-lower or all-UPPER spellings (a mixed-case one is 'Unknown command'); near-miss prefixes (?CCLEAR,ALL, ?DA, ?STAT, ?SBAUDS1,9600, ?S69600) no longer reach a setter.
?VERSION / ?version prints 'Software Version: <v>' and 'End of Version'.
